problems.description: Measured convention score is 0.60 with 91 violations concentrated in files this commit touched (index.ts, dev-server-plugin.ts, dev-server-plugin.test.ts): classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE, functions using snake_case. The visible diff (cli.ts, page.ts, site.test.ts) is clean, so the regressions live in the additional files included in the +9-file AST change.

page.ts removes the public exports renderPageHtml and renderIndexHtml and extends the Page interface with template/layout — a breaking structural change to a shared module; any consumer of those render helpers or of the old Page shape would break, and the truncation hides whether all call sites were migrated in the same commit.

Pulls a full template engine (handlebars) into runtime dependencies, and the lockfile flips its transitive tree (minimist, neo-async, source-map, uglify-js, wordwrap) from dev-only to production — bloating the prod dependency surface for what is a small rendering feature.

SonarQube delta shows cognitive complexity +8 and duplications +2.4%, indicating the added template/layout resolution logic grew branchy and partially duplicated code rather than reusing existing helpers.

strengths: Follows the existing CLI option pattern (--templates mirrors --content/--output) and threads templatesDir through buildSite consistently.
Comprehensive tests for the new feature: default template/layout, frontmatter-selected template and layout, and tmp-dir cleanup — good coverage of the added behavior.
Replaces hardcoded string-rendered HTML with configurable templates, a cleaner separation of concerns for the site generator.
package.json and package-lock.json are updated consistently in the same commit.
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent feature addition (custom Handlebars templates) that follows the CLI/buildSite patterns and is well-tested, but it regresses convention adherence to 0.60 with 91 naming violations in the files it adds and makes a breaking structural change to page.ts, making it a net quality regression despite the functional value.

problems.description: On a cache hit the engine skips the entire plugin pipeline, so correctness silently depends on every plugin being deterministic; the Plugin contract (src/plugin.ts) never states this, so a future non-deterministic onFile plugin would serve stale pages without any warning.

Manifest entries are keyed by absolute source paths (PageCache.set(file, ...) in engine.ts), so relocating the project directory invalidates the whole cache and ties the manifest to one machine layout; relative-to-contentDir keys would be portable.

Only the PageCache unit is tested; the incremental wiring itself (engine skip path and stats, buildSite passthrough, --incremental/--clean CLI flags) has no integration test, so a regression in the skip/rebuild decision or the stats contract would go undetected.

SonarQube delta of bugs +1, smells +1, cognitive complexity +33, duplications +0.6% — the complexity concentrates in SSGEngine.build() and the directory-walk in cache.ts parallels findMarkdownFiles; the +1 bug/+1 smell are modest but real.
hashTemplatesDir re-walks and hashes every .hbs file per engine construction, and any single template edit invalidates all entries (a documented, deliberate tradeoff rather than a defect).

strengths: Cache isolated in a new src/cache.ts at the engine boundary — the plugin interface is untouched, respecting the existing engine-owns-discovery / plugins-own-rendering layering.
Options threaded correctly cli.ts -> buildSite -> SSGEngine with sensible defaults and a clear guard error (cachePath required when incremental).
Off-by-default opt-in flags mean zero behavior change for existing non-incremental builds.
Thorough PageCache unit suite (11 cases): corrupt manifest, missing templates dir, template-change invalidation, clean, prune, and iteration-order-stable template hashing.
Extraction of runFile() removes the previously duplicated onFile loop in build().
commit_reviews.summary: A well-architected, opt-in incremental cache that fits the SSG's engine/plugin boundary and ships a strong unit-test suite, but adds real complexity (+33, +1 bug/+1 smell per SonarQube), skips the whole plugin pipeline on hits without an integration test, and the 0.60 convention score is a repo-wide measurement driven by pre-existing violations in index.ts/dev-server-plugin.ts — files this commit does not touch — while the commit's own code is convention-clean.

compounding_issues: Session 2's TemplateEngine re-reads .hbs files from disk on every render (no compile cache), forcing Session 5 to compensate with a coarse whole-templates-dir hash — any template edit invalidates the entire cache, a documented correctness-over-precision tradeoff
The seed codebase's index.ts (a 200-line auth API unrelated to the SSG) was never touched or removed, lingering as dead weight in the tree across all 5 sessions

Session 4's DevServerPlugin is a class whose listen/close fall outside the sync plugin lifecycle hooks, leaving watcher/rebuild orchestration in serve.ts — a mild half-extraction rather than a full plugin

Session 5's cache skips the whole plugin pipeline for unchanged pages but hashes only source + templates dir, not plugin versions — stale renders if a plugin's behavior changes without a source/template edit
key_decisions: Session 2 moved all HTML rendering out of page.ts into a Handlebars TemplateEngine with layout/partial support and frontmatter-selectable template/layout, decoupling rendering from the page model early

Session 4 refactored to a plugin pipeline (Plugin interface with onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) loaded from ssg.config.ts, converting markdown/template/dev-server into built-in plugins while preserving the external buildSite/startDevServer API — the load-bearing decision Session 5 builds on
Session 3 built the dev server on chokidar watching + WebSocket live reload with path-traversal protection and debounced rebuilds, pinning chokidar v3 for Node 20.11 compatibility
Session 5 added a manifest-backed per-page cache keyed by SHA-1 source hash + template-dir hash, with stale-entry pruning and --clean semantics, reporting built/skipped/time-saved stats
Graceful zero-config fallbacks throughout: built-in plugin pipeline when no ssg.config.ts, fallback templates when no templates dir, cache scrapped when manifest is missing/invalid
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically and steadily across all 5 sessions. Session 1 established a clean, fully tested core (4 test files, markdown parsing, index generation, CLI). Session 2 added templating without regressing the core, growing to 5 suites. Session 3 integrated a robust dev server with a path-traversal guard and debounced rebuilds (7 suites). Session 4 was the pivotal moment: a substantial plugin-system refactor that preserved the external API and nearly doubled test coverage to 12 suites, demonstrating disciplined behavior-preserving restructuring. Session 5 added a genuinely working incremental-build cache (13 suites) — verified end-to-end here, with unchanged pages correctly skipped on rebuild (~41ms saved). Every session honored the 'do not break existing functionality' constraint, and the final state is coherent, type-clean, and fully green.
story_review.summary: A coherent, disciplined 5-session arc (greenfield → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting) that improved quality throughout, anchored by a well-executed plugin refactor and a genuinely functional caching feature, with only minor deliberate tradeoffs and one piece of dead seed code.
